To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- Meeting minutes, read-outs, summaries, agendas, briefing books and presentations for meetings of the Defense Policy Board held between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2016, including (a) the two-day meeting on China's activities in the South China Sea held in the week of 21 September 2015 and (b) the two-day meeting on Turkey and its role in countering ISIS held in the week of 11 January 2016, and in particular the written study on Turkey and ISIS and the paper on China's activities in the South China Sea prepared or circulated by Board chairman John Hamre, in unclassified or redacted form, including drafts.
- Correspondence, memoranda, notes, calendar entries and meeting invitations referencing Stuart E. Eizenstat in his capacity as a member of the Defense Policy Board, between 1 January 2014 and 31 December 2017, including his appointment paperwork, ethics and confidentiality agreements, security-clearance sponsorship, and travel authorizations and vouchers.
- Records distributed outside the Defense Policy Board that reference the Board's Turkey and ISIS study or its South China Sea recommendations, between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2016, including transmittals, cover memos and briefings to the Secretary of Defense, the Deputy Secretary of Defense, and the offices of Policy, Intelligence and Strategy.
- Records referencing the sessions of the Board's meetings in the weeks of 21 September 2015 and 11 January 2016 that were attended by the Secretary of Defense or by representatives of U.S. intelligence agencies, including agendas, attendee lists and read-outs.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- Correspondence, including emails and attachments, between Stuart E. Eizenstat and Ambassador Daniel B. Shapiro, the United States Embassy in Tel Aviv, or the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs, between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2016, including his letter of 29 June 2015 transmitting the Jewish People's Policy Institute's annual assessment of the state of the Jewish people and his recommendations for countering the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) campaign, together with any reply, routing slip, internal note or summary of the material received.
- Records referencing the Jewish People's Policy Institute (also rendered "Jewish People's Policy Institute of Jerusalem") or its annual assessment of the state of the Jewish people, between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2016, including any reference to a JPPI study of the BDS movement prepared for Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
- Notes, memoranda, cables or reports recording or summarizing meetings between Stuart E. Eizenstat and Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif in 2013 and 2014, and any transmittal or briefing of those accounts to Department of State officials.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- White House Office and National Security Council records, created between 1 January 2014 and 20 January 2017, referencing Stuart E. Eizenstat, the Jewish People's Policy Institute, or the Institute's annual assessment of the state of the Jewish people, including correspondence sent to John Podesta at his Executive Office of the President email address in November 2014, and any National Security Council or White House Office handling of the Institute's assessment transmitted to the Department of State through Ambassador Daniel B. Shapiro in 2015.
- Records, created between 1 January 2015 and 20 January 2017, referencing recommendations received from outside advisers on countering the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions campaign against Israel, including any staff summary, talking points or tasking generated in response.
- Records, created between 1 January 2015 and 20 January 2017, referencing the meetings between then-Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his cabinet and outside delegations from the Jewish People's Policy Institute held on or about 28 June 2015 and 27 June 2015, as reported to the White House.
- Records, created between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2016, transmitting or discussing the Defense Policy Board's studies on Turkey and ISIS and on China's activities in the South China Sea, where received by the National Security Council.
- Calendar entries, visitor records and meeting lists, created between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2016, recording meetings between White House or National Security Council staff and Stuart E. Eizenstat.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All contracts, licenses, MOUs, MOAs, data agreements, letters of intent, State of Work documents, Scope of Work documents, and other agreement documents with Axon, Fusus, Axis Communications, Flock Safety and LiveView Technologies that were active any time between 1/1/2020 and the date this request is fulfilled.

2. User manuals, handbooks, or comparable instructional documents provided to the department by Axon, Fusus, Axis Communications and Flock Safety and regarding Axon, Fusus, Axis Communications and Flock Safety products and services

3. Audit logs/audit trails documenting each time a department account and/or outside agency has performed a license plate reader search through the Axon, Fusus, Axis Communications, Flock Safety and LiveView Technologies platforms from 1/1/2020 until the date this request is processed.

4. A list of city-owned and/or non-city-owned devices, such as cameras, automatic license plate readers, and gunshot detection systems, registered and/or integrated with the Police Department's Axon, Fusus, Axis Communications, Flock Safety and LiveView Technologies Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC) system sufficient to discern the registration name, full street address, number of internal and external devices, whether devices are registered or integrated, and date/time created.

5. Any requests for proposals, proposals submitted by vendors, contracts, budgets or cost allocations for the purchase and/or use of aerial drones, UAs, UAVs, and UASs (hereinafter “drones”);

6. Any policies, guidelines, manuals and/or instructions on department use of drones, including on the legal process required (such as a warrant or court order), if any, before operating a drone;

7. Any departmental records concerning this department’s use of drones now or plans to use drones in the future including:

a. The types of investigations or instances in which this department is using or plans to use drones, or how it plans to support, manage or oversee the usage of drones by another department or office;

b. policies, guidelines, manuals and/or instructions on storage requirements or procedures for video or static images obtained through use of drones, including retention times;

c. The altitude at which drones can or do fly

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Stephen Bourn
